name: A Solar Tale (HerCode Space)
tagline: A digital children's story narrated by the Sun that explains how space weather touches daily life, with science sourced from NASA and NOAA.
problem: Space weather affects technology and daily life on Earth, but it is invisible and abstract, especially for children.
solution: A scroll-driven, mobile-first web story in five poetic acts told by the Sun — from ancient myths and Galileo's telescope to modern solar flares and a curious girl — that introduces a space-weather concept in each act, for classrooms, libraries and outreach programs.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the project that most creatively communicates the potential of open data through storytelling.
Pairs real heliophysics with vibrant illustrations for a named audience (kids) and named channels (classrooms, libraries, outreach).
A clear narrative device — the Sun as narrator across five acts — carries science, history and myth in one arc.
Treats data trust as a design rule: every scientific reference comes from NASA or NOAA.
A storytelling challenge rewarded a media artifact built on data — a lane most developer teams skip.

lessons: Storytelling challenges are winnable without heavy code: pick a named audience, a narrator and a channel.
Keep the science real and cite it; the story must rest on the actual data.
If generative tools make the illustrations or voice, disclose them as the rules require.
